answer: An agent marketplace selling tundra maps, vine cuttings, and opal assigns voting power in proportion to collateral locked for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities gives exactly the same total voting power as one identity holding 100 tokens. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral, paying its purchase or borrowing cost and giving up other uses of that capital during the lock.
